text:
Nikolaj Ehlers came to Carolina as a shooter and has turned into one of the league's best feeders. He has 20 points in 21 games but only five goals, and his last ten games produced 12 points (two goals, ten assists) against the 8.6 our numbers would expect at his ice time.

That's not hard to believe once you look at how he plays. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 97th percentile among forwards in primary shot assists last season, carrying the puck in on 61% of his entries, with more than half his shots coming off the rush. Evolving-Hockey ranked him 16th of 401 forwards by wins above replacement, with real defensive value too.

The funny part is that he's only playing 16:17 a night, and half his points have come on the power play. The goals should come closer to his chances (5 on 5.8 expected), and the Hurricanes have won eight of his last ten. A Stanley Cup ring from last spring and a trip home to the Global Series in Finland: it's a good stretch to be Nikolaj Ehlers.
headline: Ehlers, the setup man in Carolina
